questions.explanation: ML-KEM (formerly CRYSTALS-Kyber) is standardized under FIPS 203 for key exchange.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm is standardized under FIPS 205 as a conservative hash-based backup?
questions.explanation: SLH-DSA (formerly SPHINCS+) is the hash-based signature standard under FIPS 205, intended as a diversified backup.

questions.prompt: What is the default choice for general-purpose PQC signatures per algorithm selection guidance?
questions.explanation: ML-DSA is the default choice for general-purpose signatures, balancing size and performance well.

questions.prompt: Why should PQC standards content always be verified against nist.gov before publishing?
options: It never changes so verification is unnecessary
Standardization is an ongoing process and content can go stale
Standards are only relevant to symmetric cryptography
questions.explanation: PQC standardization is an active, ongoing process — content should always be checked against current official sources rather than assumed static.

questions.prompt: What practical concern does protocol-level negotiation address for PQC deployment?
options: How a client and server agree on and advertise PQC algorithm support during a handshake
The physical color of network cables
questions.explanation: Protocol-level negotiation covers how systems like TLS advertise and agree on PQC algorithm support between client and server.
